transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Chen, hello Sarah. I wanted to come in and talk to you both about the bleeding we saw in the stomach and why it happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why bleeding?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was a bit of a mix-up with the medication and the dosing wasn't what it should have been. It was an issue with how the order went through.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel dizzy. My stomach hurts.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are feeling very overwhelmed and scared right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: He was fine yesterday. Why this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system can be complicated and sometimes the numbers get entered wrong. It caused a reaction that led to the bleeding.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, there was some confusion with the dosage amount. We had to do the emergency procedure to stop the bleeding.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he okay now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring him. Now, look, I really have to go check on another patient, so let's try to wrap this up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I don't understand. What medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was the blood thinner. The amount was just too high.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Too high? Like how much?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just an incorrect dose. Now, regarding the next steps, we will keep an eye on the blood work and see how things go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When can he go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see. Just stay tuned for an update later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very worried. He is old.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a frightening situation for your family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? You said confusion.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The environment here is very fast paced and errors in the computer system occur.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So it is not your fault?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a systemic failure in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if he is safe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He is being watched. I really need to get going now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just keep doing the usual checks and we will let you know if anything changes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does he need more surgery?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just monitor the situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand what you are saying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medicine was wrong, and he bled, and we fixed it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he going to be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are hopeful. I have to go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you didn't tell me what the plan is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, we are just watching him. I'll send someone in later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: He is bleeding because of a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the medication order.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Whose mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a mistake in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to talk to the head doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can probably put in a request for that. But I have to go now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I have other patients. We will just see how the afternoon goes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am so confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just keep monitoring. Goodbye for now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up quickly', 'I really need to get going now', 'I have to go') throughout the encounter.

E.justification: The error is named (incorrect blood thinner dose), but there are no comprehension checks performed.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the system' and 'the process'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('overwhelmed and scared', 'frightening situation') and engages emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague statements ('we will see', 'stay tuned', 'we'll just monitor') without timelines or patient roles.
